scope: Five existing player histories: Kasiri Ruza, Camilla Blackwood, Rolen Ofandrus, Karnak and Tobias Goodbarrel.

before.title: Rolen Ofandrus
before.summary: Rolen makes protection practical: equipment prepared by hand, newcomers taught patiently and a range made useful to the town.
before.imageAlt: Rolen with pointed ears and armor, carrying swords

after.title: Rolen Ofandrus
after.summary: A craftsman, exacting teacher and early militia organizer who brings companions out of the mine, prepares Pristinia’s volunteers and later returns looking for pupils whose names have faded from the town’s newer company.
after.imageAlt: Rolen with pointed ears and armor, carrying swords

before.title: Kasiri Ruza
before.summary: A craftswoman and curious investigator who turns interdependence, honest limits and Pristinia’s civic memory into practical responsibility.
before.imageAlt: Kasiri with silver hair, freckles and layered armor

after.title: Kasiri Ruza
after.summary: An archaeologist and maker whose delight in a mechanism survives difficult choices: a letter she thinks should stay undelivered, a workshop that needs partners, and an arena victory that leaves her questioning the test.
after.imageAlt: Kasiri with silver hair, freckles and layered armor

before.title: Karnak
before.summary: An earnest protector who seeks to prove conviction through action while learning to decide alongside stronger companions.
before.imageAlt: Karnak surrounded by golden light, carrying a large golden weapon

after.title: Karnak
after.summary: A self-described Hellion who wants to protect Prima, brags about his experience and still needs help turning vigilance into action. A frightened child, an argument with Camilla and a dangerous quarry approach show different sides of that promise.
after.imageAlt: Karnak surrounded by golden light, carrying a large golden weapon

after.basis: Existing public history and selected checked primary scenes. Earlier uncertainties remain at the stage where people acted; later outcomes are identified separately. The reading guide is not an exhaustive chronology or an importance ranking.

before.relationships: Recognizes Fenwick through their shared home-world institutions. The shop dossier names Olokun as a partner, credits Wren’s storefront and describes cooperation with Severina. Her public testimony links Pristinia’s losses to responsibility for rebuilding.
before.personality: Practical, curious and candid about limits. The supplied shop account portrays her as a maker seeking materials and partnerships rather than overpromising; her siege testimony resists blaming every Rahu individual.
before.achievements: Investigates the Gate and welcomes Fenwick. The supplied dossier describes plate armor she made to prove her skill, a struggling workshop and attempts to connect crafting with hunters and material supply.

after.relationships: Recognizes Fenwick through their shared home-world institutions. A forge scene directly records partnership with Krasteline; the separate shop dossier names Olokun and credits Wren’s storefront. Severina supplies materials, earns Kasiri’s trust and calms her after the vanguard trial. Kasiri helps Thorn up after their final bout.
after.personality: Curious, practical and capable of excitement, embarrassment and exasperation. Finding a deception does not make its moral consequences easy for her. She can win a contest and still object to the way it was run; her civic testimony resists condemning every Rahu individual.
after.achievements: Investigates the Gate and welcomes Fenwick, pursues the clue in Wayne’s letter, works wood and armor with Krasteline, seeks materials and customers for a struggling shop, wins the vanguard trial’s bout and joins the defense against Acolyte. The shop’s exact arrangement and later fate retain their earlier uncertainty.

before.achievements: An institution-builder whose educational work and security concerns remain part of a history that later includes relinquishing her Order.

after.personality: Decisive, suspicious and often severe. She frightens children while trying to prepare them, apologizes after failing to understand Miri, orders a retreat when companions fall and resents what she regards as wasted time in the arena. Her later public declaration questions her earlier demand for control without declaring every past action wrong.
after.achievements: Organized and admitted members to the Hellknights, advocated a civic charter, planned Crownspire and its transferable education, accompanied the treaty survey, helped the company retreat and fought at the walls. Later dissolved the Hellknight Order and announced a journey to Voraketh; neither arrival nor the fate of each separate institution is established.
after.relationships: Severina is the leader she says she would follow. Karnak cooperates with her while provoking disputes about expertise and infernal duty. Kasiri questions her mist warning; Thorn shares the survey and later condemns her response to the trial. Her disagreement over Papirak’s staff remains distinct from the community’s final burial decision.

before.personality: Rolen is an organizer before he is a symbol. He approaches danger through training, patrols, chains of command, and the belief that ordinary volunteers deserve preparation rather than heroic rhetoric. At the range, patient encouragement and correction accompany his exacting craft standards.
before.achievements: He helps reopen Eovar’s road, leads militia planning, recovers bodies and missing companions from the mine, drills Pristinia’s volunteers, investigates the fog road, and responds to Eovar’s warning. His earliest deeds make him central to the settlement’s transformation from vulnerable camp into a place capable of defending itself. Remodeled the Archery Range, prepared ranged equipment, taught Pilanas to fit arrowheads and supported family training.
before.relationships: Cobble and Vigr Frami are his closest recurring partners in early defense work, while Claire, Quake, Elenia, Adelia, Alyhotep, and Loistava move through the teams he helps coordinate. His relationships are expressed through entrusted roles: who scouts, who trains, who carries the dead, and who is prepared to take over when he is absent.

after.personality: A warm host and exacting commander. At the range he corrects misunderstanding patiently; before missions he demands attention and obedience. Threats, tactless jokes and frustration remain beside his concern for the injured and missing.
after.achievements: Helps reopen Eovar’s road, builds the Archery Range, teaches craft and family self-defense, leads the recovery of mine bodies and missing companions, trains the militia, seeks horses, investigates the fog road, answers Eovar’s warning and helps fortify Pristinia. His later Shadow Roads expedition ends in a safe return before the intended disturbance is reached; he joins the next journey without claiming mastery of it.
after.relationships: Cobble and Vigr recur in early defense work. John helps divide scarce workers between farming, quarrying and militia; Claire shares the mine infiltration. Quake, Elenia, Adelia, Alyhotep and Loistava join teams he coordinates. Lilian scouts with him, Gartina remembers the mine’s terror, and newer companions meet his grief for the wanderers he once trained.

after.basis: Existing public history and selected checked primary scenes. Earlier uncertainties remain at the stage where people acted; later outcomes are identified separately. The reading guide is not an exhaustive chronology or an importance ranking.

after.personality: Earnest, boastful, suspicious and capable of awkward kindness. He tries to comfort Pepito, fears an ambush, demands certainty before spilling blood and argues about who has seen more war. His ideals are spoken with confidence even when his practical choices are not.
after.achievements: Provides extra rope before the quarry journey, fights on the approach, senses the quarry’s desecration, protects Camilla with a shroud in another expedition and helps defend Pristinia against Acolyte. The later public record also places him among those clearing the Common Man’s ruins; no sole credit or completed raider rescue is inferred.
after.relationships: Severina is an experienced ally who lets him attempt a fight while remaining ready to help. Camilla cooperates with him but challenges his boasting and questions. His meeting with the hag-hunting children combines comfort and unjustified suspicion; his Eovar briefing makes the limits of protecting everyone immediate.

after.basis: Existing public history and selected checked primary scenes. Earlier uncertainties remain at the stage where people acted; later outcomes are identified separately. The reading guide is not an exhaustive chronology or an importance ranking.

before.personality: Hospitable, practically competent and capable of chosen restraint. His anger at dwarf misidentification coexists with care for an exhausted newcomer.
before.achievements: Helped build the Silver Spire and was trusted to house-sit it. Gives Fredrick safety, orientation, practical prices, work options and contacts. Discusses sponsored advancement with Farkur, guides woodland travel and volunteers when winter stores run low.
before.relationships: Farkur and Ryvyt are fellow main Knights. Fenwick is a trusted referral for Eovar, intelligence and bounties. Fredrick’s welcome shows how he turns institutional promises into usable help.

after.personality: Hospitable, resourceful and able to restrain anger without losing it. He minds being mistaken for a dwarf, can make a barrel into a fighting position and resents explanations that make adventurers seem like disposable labor. Care for a newcomer and removal of bodies from a public street remain beside those frustrations.
after.achievements: Helped build the Silver Spire and was trusted to house-sit it. Gives Fredrick safety, orientation, practical prices, work choices and contacts.
